summary: Specifies functions for MPLS Transport Profile OAM: continuity check to spot lost connectivity, connectivity verification to confirm source and sink match, and remote defect indication to report faults back to the other end. It was later updated by RFC 7214.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC defines checks for MPLS-TP paths. Repeating BFD messages help detect silence, confirm that the far end is the expected endpoint, and report a fault to the peer.

questions: how does bfd work with mpls-tp
subtitle: Uses BFD messages to check MPLS-TP continuity, verify the far-end identity and report defects.

tldr.problem: MPLS-TP circuits need to detect lost continuity, a connection to the wrong endpoint and faults seen by the far end.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC combines continuity-check and connectivity-verification packets in one BFD session; verification packets carry a source endpoint identifier, and defect reports use BFD diagnostics.
tldr.outcome: It defines the BFD profile and message formats for these checks. RFC 7214 later updates it.

today: RFC 6428 is a Proposed Standard and is updated by RFC 7214.

sections.title: Three Operations and Maintenance Checks
sections.content:
Continuity Check (CC) detects loss of continuity on a path. Connectivity Verification (CV) confirms that the intended source connects to the intended sink. Remote Defect Indication (RDI) lets one endpoint report a fault to its peer.

This RFC uses Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) for these functions on pseudowires, Label Switched Paths and sections. It applies to bidirectional paths and BFD asynchronous mode; procedures for unidirectional and point-to-multipoint paths are left for further study.
sections.plainLanguage: The checks answer three questions: is the path still connected, is it connected to the right endpoint, and has the other end detected a fault?

sections.title: One BFD Session for CC and CV
sections.content:
CC and CV packets share one BFD session and are distinguished by Associated Channel Header code points. CC packets carry BFD control data. CV packets add a Source MEP-ID TLV so the receiving endpoint can check where the packet came from.

CV packets are inserted once per second. Loss of continuity is declared when the BFD detection time expires; the Detect Multiplier is set to 3 for the CC code point. RDI is carried in the diagnostic field of CC messages, not as a separate packet.
sections.plainLanguage: The endpoints send ordinary check messages and occasional messages with a source identifier. That identifier helps the receiver detect traffic arriving from the wrong path.

sections.title: CC and CV Message Contents
sections.content:
A CC message contains an Associated Channel Header followed by a BFD control packet. Its code point is 0x0022. A CV message uses code point 0x0023 and adds a Source MEP-ID TLV after the BFD control packet.

The TLV identifies a section, LSP or pseudowire endpoint. A node must not change the source identifier. The BFD control packet's length does not include the TLV.
sections.plainLanguage: Both message types carry BFD control data. A CV message also carries an identifier for the sending maintenance endpoint.

sections.title: Session Behavior and Defect Handling
sections.content:
A BFD session starts when the operator enables CC and CV for a maintenance entity and ends when those functions are disabled. All BFD state changes and Poll/Final exchanges use CC packets; receivers ignore that information in CV packets.

A timeout, Link Down Indication or Lock Report can signal a continuity defect. Unexpected encapsulation, endpoint identity, discriminator, label or authentication can signal mis-connectivity. On mis-connectivity, the endpoint discards non-OAM traffic and reports diagnostic code 9; the defect clears after 3.5 seconds without a defective CV message.
sections.plainLanguage: If messages stop or identify the wrong endpoint, the receiver reports a defect. It stops forwarding ordinary traffic when it detects mis-connectivity.

sections.title: Security and Identifier Registration
sections.content:
Connectivity verification helps detect traffic leaking between paths. BFD authentication may be used; the RFC describes how the expected endpoint identifier is linked to the authenticated session discriminator.

The RFC uses globally unique endpoint identifiers to detect persistent leaks. If two misconnected paths share identifiers, a leak may go undetected. IANA assigned channel types 0x0022 and 0x0023, and diagnostic code 9 for mis-connectivity.
sections.plainLanguage: Endpoint identifiers help reveal traffic sent along the wrong path. Reusing identifiers can make some misconnections harder to detect.
